daten.beratung.anliegen.0.text: When the issue is not the contour of the face but the surface — radiance, texture, pores, fine crêpey lines — then it is a matter of skin quality. That calls for different procedures than sagging does, and they usually require several sessions.
daten.beratung.anliegen.0.titel: My skin looks tired and dull
daten.beratung.anliegen.1.text: A jawline that is losing definition, cheeks that have dropped, jowls beginning to form: here the degree decides. Where sagging is just beginning, non-surgical procedures are an option; where there is clearly excess skin, a facelift is the honest answer — anything else would be money spent for a year.
daten.beratung.anliegen.10.text: The decisive difference: is it the eyelid or the brow? A simple test — gently lift the brow with your finger. If the eye already looks awake, the brow is the issue, and an eyelid lift would be the wrong procedure.
daten.beratung.anliegen.11.text: Too dark, chipped, crooked, or all of these together? If the teeth are healthy and merely discoloured, whitening is enough and costs no tooth substance. If they are healthy but crooked, orthodontic treatment is gentler. Only where substance is missing are veneers or crowns the right answer — and what is removed does not come back.
daten.beratung.anliegen.11.titel: I don't like showing my teeth
daten.beratung.anliegen.12.text: Laser works through the pigment in the hair. Dark hair responds well; blond, red and grey hair barely at all. It is a permanent reduction of hair, not permanent freedom from hair — and it takes six to ten sessions.
daten.beratung.anliegen.2.text: Lines that appear when you speak and laugh come from the muscle underneath. Lines that remain even when the face is relaxed come from the skin. Botox is intended for the one, fillers or laser for the other. That distinction belongs at the beginning of the consultation, not at the end.
daten.beratung.anliegen.2.titel: My frown and forehead lines bother me
daten.beratung.anliegen.3.text: Over the years volume is lost — in the cheeks, in the temples, under the eyes. Fillers give it back. The most common mistake here is too much: an over-plumped face looks older, not younger.
daten.beratung.anliegen.4.text: The first question is whether hair follicles are still present. Where they are weakened, non-surgical treatments are an option; where they are missing, only a transplant helps. The two do not rule each other out — and with hereditary hair loss it should be discussed in parallel what will slow the further loss.
daten.beratung.anliegen.5.text: Hair loss in women is more often diffuse than in men, and it often has a treatable cause: iron, thyroid, hormones, medication. That is why a proper work-up belongs before any transplant — otherwise you are transplanting into an ongoing process.
daten.beratung.anliegen.6.text: Where skin is left over and the straight abdominal muscles have separated, no amount of training will change it. Where only isolated fat deposits are the problem and the skin is firm, liposuction is the smaller procedure. The condition for both: stable weight and completed family planning.
daten.beratung.anliegen.6.titel: My stomach has not gone back after pregnancy
daten.beratung.anliegen.7.text: If the rest of your body responds to exercise and diet and one area does not, the question is shape, not weight. None of these procedures helps with weight loss — and anyone who comes with that expectation risks having too much done.
daten.beratung.anliegen.7.titel: Isolated fat deposits won't go away
daten.beratung.anliegen.8.text: Two different questions: is volume missing, or has the breast dropped? An augmentation creates volume but no lift; a lift creates shape but no volume. Anyone who wants both needs both — with correspondingly more effort and more risk.
daten.beratung.anliegen.9.text: Is it about a hump, a deviation or the tip — and do you breathe well? Small irregularities can be evened out without surgery using fillers, to a limited extent and for a limited time. Everything beyond that, and above all anything to do with breathing, is a surgical procedure.
daten.beratung.lokale_alternative.hinwei: Content finding B12, point 4: “This treatment is also available in St. Margrethen” is currently shown as a grey information box for 20 of 101 treatments. This is not small print but the strongest consulting argument ETA has: “For this treatment you don't have to fly.” An agency that occasionally advises against the journey becomes more credible, not less.
daten.beratung.lokale_alternative.text: Our aftercare partner Riverside Beauty also offers this treatment in St. Margrethen. For a treatment of this scale a journey is usually not worthwhile — we will gladly tell you what makes more sense in your case.
daten.beratung.vergleiche.gruppen.haartr: All four are variants of the same basic method: individual extraction from the donor area at the back and sides, implantation in the thinning area. The difference lies in the instrument. Sapphire concerns the blade used to open the channels; DHI concerns the implanter pen used to place the hair. Broadly: classic FUE for large areas, DHI for the hairline and for densification between existing hair. Anyone who sells you one of the variants as generally the better one without looking at your findings is selling, not advising. The figure you use to compare offers is the same in all four cases: grafts.
FUE, DHI, sapphire and percutaneous compared
daten.beratung.vergleiche.gruppen.haut-b: All four tighten without surgery, but they do different things. HIFU works over a whole area through newly formed collagen, with no downtime and a slow build-up over two to three months. Threads lift mechanically and take effect immediately, but cost a few days of swelling. Radiofrequency with microneedling additionally targets skin quality. Mesolifting is mainly hydration and only tightens to a limited degree. None of them replaces a facelift where there is clearly excess skin — that is the sentence a consultation has to say when it applies.
HIFU, threads, radiofrequency and mesolifting compared
daten.beratung.vergleiche.gruppen.plasti: Volume and shape are two different questions. An implant gives volume and usually lasts ten to fifteen years — factor in a replacement. Fat transfer works without foreign material, but only by a bare cup size per session, and part of it is reabsorbed. A lift raises and shapes, but does not fill.
Augmentation, lift and fat transfer compared

The question is not how much fat should come off, but how well the skin retracts. If it is firm, liposuction is enough. If it has lost its tone, liposuction leaves an empty envelope, and the right answer is a tightening procedure — with a scar. Both procedures require a stable weight, and both carry the highest risk of thrombosis in this catalogue.
daten.beratung.vergleiche.gruppen.zaehne: Sorted by how much tooth substance you lose in the process: whitening costs none. A veneer costs a little enamel. A crown requires the tooth to be ground down all round — and that is final. An implant replaces a tooth that is already missing. With every package offer, ask whether veneers or crowns are planned; many offers work with crowns to save time, and the difference is considerable.
Whitening, veneers, crowns and implants compared
daten.beratung.verwandte_behandlungen.hi: Content findings B5 and B12: no treatment page currently links to a related treatment. Anyone who lands on “thread lift” has no route to “HIFU” other than through the menu. The assignment is held per treatment in data/behandlungsdaten.json → verwandt and is derived from group membership, so it is complete for all 101 treatments.

daten.risiken-gruppen.gruppen.haartransp: Autologous blood, active-substance and pigmentation treatments for the hair carry little risk. With the injection-based procedures, however, effectiveness is not established by robust studies, and some of those treated do not respond. That belongs said before the decision, not afterwards.

These procedures can support existing, weakened hair follicles or make the hair look denser. Where there are no hair follicles left, none of them will make hair grow. Pigmentation creates the impression of density, but it is colour in the skin, not hair — and it has to be refreshed.
Non-surgical hair treatments
a feeling of pressure, redness and slight swelling of the scalp for a few hours
small bruises at the injection sites
headache on the day of treatment
with pigmentation: redness and crusting for a few days
infection at the injection sites
allergic reaction to active substances or pigments
with pigmentation: a shift in colour towards blue or red over the years, uneven fading, the need for touch-ups
no response at all
Risks and limits of non-surgical hair treatments
Seek medical advice promptly if redness increases with warmth, pus or fever. The same applies to a spreading rash.

A hair transplant is a comparatively low-risk procedure under local anaesthetic. The most common disappointments are not medical but a question of expectation: about density, about timing, and about the fact that your own hair loss continues after the procedure.

What is transplanted is the donor hair you already have, not new hair. The density of your hair at twenty cannot be restored with it, and the donor area is finite. Hereditary hair loss continues after the procedure: without accompanying treatment, the result can look patchy again after some years, even though the grafts hold. The result can be judged at the earliest after twelve months.
Hair transplantation
swelling of the forehead and eyelids in the first three to five days
crusts and redness in the recipient area for ten to fourteen days
numbness at the donor and recipient sites for weeks to months
shock loss: temporary loss of existing hair in the treated area as well
pinpoint scars in the donor area
inflammation of individual hair follicles (folliculitis)
infection or impaired wound healing
secondary bleeding
uneven density, a hairline that does not suit the face, or hair growing in the wrong direction
a poor growth rate with noticeably less hair than expected
visible over-harvesting of the donor area if too many grafts were taken — this cannot be corrected
raised scarring in those predisposed to it
Risks and limits of hair transplants

Seek medical advice promptly in the event of: fever, increasing redness with warmth, pus at the donor or recipient site, severe or increasing pain, persistent bleeding. Swelling of the forehead in the first few days, by contrast, is normal.
daten.risiken-gruppen.gruppen.haut-beaut: Botulinum toxin has been used in medicine for decades and is considered well tolerated when applied properly and dosed correctly. That does not make it free of risk. Most unwanted effects are temporary, because the substance itself is broken down after a few months.

Botulinum toxin relaxes muscles. It therefore works on lines caused by facial expression — not on lines already etched into a relaxed face, not on slack skin and not on loss of volume. Anyone expecting a firm facial contour is expecting something from the wrong procedure.
Botox
small bruises and redness at the injection sites, usually for one to two days
headache or a feeling of pressure in the first few days
a slight feeling of heaviness or tightness in the treated area
a drooping upper eyelid or a lowered brow if the substance migrates into neighbouring muscles — this resolves by itself over some weeks, but is clearly visible until then
asymmetrical facial expression where the distribution is uneven
difficulty swallowing or speaking after treatment in the neck or jaw area
allergic reactions
a decline in the effect with very frequent use, through the formation of antibodies
Risks and limits of botulinum toxin treatments

In the event of shortness of breath, difficulty swallowing, blurred or double vision or pronounced muscle weakness, seek medical help immediately. In the event of a drooping eyelid or marked asymmetry, contact the treating practice within a few days.

This group covers very different procedures — from professional cleansing treatments through peels and micro-injuries to injections of active substances. The risks differ accordingly. What they have in common: for several of these procedures the effect is not established by robust studies, and that belongs said before you decide.

These procedures improve the appearance, hydration and surface of the skin. They do not lift tissue that has dropped and are no substitute for a tightening procedure. For the regenerative procedures (autologous blood, polynucleotides, stem cell preparations) there is a further point: some of those treated do not respond, and a lack of success is not a treatment error. Ask about the preparation, the manufacturer and its regulatory status.
Skin rejuvenation & care
redness, swelling and a feeling of tightness for hours to a few days
flaking and dryness after peels
small bruises and weals after injections
a temporary worsening of the skin's appearance in the first week
infection at injection or treatment sites
persistent redness, pigment changes or scarring after deep peels and in darker skin types
reactivation of herpes
allergic or delayed foreign-body reaction, depending on the preparation
no response at all
Risks and limits of skin rejuvenation and care treatments

If redness increases with warmth, pus forms or you have a fever, seek medical advice within a few days. If a spreading blistering rash appears, think of a herpes reactivation and have it treated quickly.

Hyaluronic acid fillers are considered comparatively safe because the material can be dissolved again with an antidote. The most serious complication — accidental blockage of a blood vessel — is rare, but serious, and has to be treated immediately. Before the treatment, ask whether the antidote hyaluronidase is kept in stock at the practice.

Fillers add volume and redefine contours. They do not tighten slack skin, are no substitute for a lift and improve skin quality only to a limited degree. Too much material leads to an over-plumped face that looks older rather than younger — here, less is regularly more.
Hyaluronic acid & fillers
swelling and bruising for a few days
tenderness to pressure in the treated area
palpable irregularities or small nodules, which usually resolve
asymmetry, which can be corrected afterwards

vascular occlusion: the filler enters a vessel and interrupts the blood supply. The consequences can be tissue death and — with injections in the nose and eye region — visual disturbance up to blindness.
infection or abscess at the injection site
delayed foreign-body reaction with nodules forming weeks to months later
reactivation of cold sores
allergic reaction to components of the preparation
Risks and limits of hyaluronic acid injections

Return to the practice or go to an emergency department immediately in the event of: increasing, severe pain after the treatment, whitening or blotchy, net-like discolouration of the skin, sudden visual disturbance. These are the signs of a vascular occlusion, and it can be treated if you are quick — every hour counts. In the event of fever, warmth or pus, report within a few days.

Cold, heat, massage and injections change small, circumscribed fat deposits. None of these procedures is a means of losing weight, and none replaces liposuction. That is not a cautionary formula but the most common reason for disappointment in this group.

These procedures shape small areas at a stable weight. They do not help with weight loss, do not tighten slack skin and do not work in everyone treated. For larger volumes, liposuction is the appropriate procedure — and for weight, diet is.
Body contouring
redness, swelling and tenderness to pressure for days
numbness in the treated area for days to weeks
bruises and hardened areas
with injections: marked swelling over several days up to two weeks
paradoxical increase in fatty tissue after cryolipolysis — a rare but documented reaction in which the treated area becomes larger instead of smaller and has to be corrected surgically
frostbite or burning of the skin
nodules, irregularities and dents
infection or abscess after injections
tissue death if the injection depth is wrong
no response at all
Risks and limits of non-surgical body contouring treatments

If redness increases with warmth, pus or fever, seek medical advice immediately. The same applies to open areas or blisters. If a treated area becomes firmer and larger instead of smaller after some weeks, get in touch — that may be a paradoxical reaction.

Lasers work with light that is absorbed by a particular pigment in the skin — by hair pigment, by tattoo ink, by the pigment in blood or by the water in the skin. All the risks in this group depend on how well the device, the settings and the skin type fit together. The single most important factor you can influence yourself: tanned skin markedly increases the risk of burns.

Laser treatments act on the surface of the skin and its upper layers. They do not tighten tissue that has dropped and are no substitute for fillers or a lift. For hair removal the rule is: it is a permanent reduction of hair, not permanent freedom from hair — blond, red and grey hairs barely respond. For tattoo removal, several sessions are needed, and some colours cannot be removed completely.
Laser treatments
redness, swelling and a feeling of warmth for hours to days
crusting after ablative treatments
temporary darkening or lightening of the treated skin
pain during the treatment
burns with blistering
permanent pigment change, particularly in darker skin types and on tanned skin
scarring, usually as a consequence of a burn or an infection
infection or herpes reactivation after ablative procedures
eye damage without correct eye protection
paradoxical hair growth at the edge of the treated area during hair removal
Risks and limits of laser and light treatments
In the event of blisters, open areas, increasing redness with warmth, pus or fever, seek medical advice promptly. In the event of visual disturbance after a treatment on the face, immediately.

Ultrasound, radiofrequency and thread lifts work beneath the surface of the skin without opening it. The risks are correspondingly lower than with surgery — but so is the effect. The most common harm with these procedures is not medical but an expectation the procedure cannot meet.

These procedures tighten existing tissue and stimulate the formation of collagen. They do not remove excess skin. Where there is marked sagging with excess skin, a surgical facelift is the honest answer — and anyone who sells you a thread lift as an alternative on those findings is selling you time, not a result.
Non-surgical tightening
redness, swelling and tenderness to pressure for hours to days
pain during the treatment, at times considerable with ultrasound
temporary tingling or numbness
with threads: pulling and a feeling of tightness for one to two weeks
burns or blistering if the energy setting is wrong
temporary nerve irritation with weakness of facial expression
loss of fatty tissue in the treated area if the energy is too high, which makes the face look hollow
with threads: visible or palpable threads, dents along the line of the thread, a thread slipping, infection at an entry point
no response at all — these procedures do not work the same way in everyone
Risks and limits of non-surgical tightening procedures

In the event of blisters, open areas, increasing redness with warmth, or newly occurring weakness of facial expression, seek medical advice promptly. With threads: report immediately in the event of fever or pus at an entry point.
daten.risiken-gruppen.gruppen.medizinisc: These entries describe specialist departments of the partner clinic, not individual treatments. Which examination or treatment makes sense in your case follows from the medical assessment on site. ETA arranges and organises; the medical decision is taken by the doctor.

For examinations and treatments covered by your health insurance in Switzerland, treatment abroad is usually not the sensible route — cover abroad is tied to narrow conditions and has to be clarified beforehand. Speak to your family doctor first.
Notes on the medical specialist departments
In the event of acute symptoms, contact your family doctor in Switzerland or the emergency department. A planned treatment abroad is no substitute for an urgent assessment at home.
daten.risiken-gruppen.gruppen.plastische: Breast operations are well-established procedures with a high proportion of satisfied patients. They are at the same time procedures with late consequences that can appear years later — with implants, capsular contracture; with lifts, renewed dropping. Anyone planning one of these procedures is also planning for a possible second operation.

An augmentation creates volume but no lift; a lift creates shape but no volume. Implants are not a state that lasts for ever — reckon on a replacement or removal at some point, along with the cost. And: pregnancy, breastfeeding and fluctuations in weight change every operated breast again.
Breast
swelling, a feeling of tightness and pain in the first few days
restricted arm movement for one to two weeks
altered sensation in the nipple and skin, usually receding
scars that fade over twelve to eighteen months
secondary bleeding or a collection of blood requiring a further operation
infection — particularly serious with implants, because it may force their removal
capsular contracture: hardening of the connective-tissue capsule around the implant, so that the breast becomes firm, painful or deformed; the most common late complication, often only after years
permanent loss of sensation in the nipple
reduced or lost ability to breastfeed
impaired blood supply to the nipple or areola, up to loss of tissue
rupture of an implant, slipping, or visible edges and rippling
BIA-ALCL, a very rare form of lymph gland cancer associated with certain textured implants
more difficult interpretation of mammograms
general anaesthetic risks as well as thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
Risks and limits of breast operations

Seek medical help immediately in the event of: rapidly increasing one-sided swelling or pain in the first few days, fever above 38.5 degrees, redness with warmth or pus, shortness of breath or chest pain, a swollen and painful leg on one side. Seek medical assessment — even years later — in the event of: newly occurring hardening, a change in shape, persistent pain or sudden swelling of the breast.

Every operation on the face brings two kinds of risk: the general risks of an operation and an anaesthetic, and the particular ones of this region — visible scars, the nerve branches for facial expression, and the fact that a result on the face cannot be hidden. With all procedures in this group, reckon on two to three weeks of visible swelling and discolouration.

An operation changes the shape and position of tissue. It does not improve skin quality: pigment spots, fine crêpey lines and sun damage remain. It does not stop ageing, it turns the clock back. And it cannot fulfil the idea created by an edited picture — what is possible is determined by your bone structure, the thickness of your skin and the way you heal.
Face
swelling and bruising for two to three weeks
numbness in the operated area for weeks to months
a feeling of tightness and strangeness
scars that fade over twelve to eighteen months, but remain
secondary bleeding or a collection of blood that may make a further operation necessary — usually in the first few hours
infection or impaired wound healing, considerably more common in smokers
injury to a branch of the facial nerve with temporary or, rarely, permanent weakness of facial expression
asymmetry or a result that does not match expectations
raised or widened scars
the need for a corrective procedure
general anaesthetic risks as well as thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
Risks and limits of surgical procedures on the face

Seek medical help immediately in the event of: rapidly increasing one-sided swelling or pain in the first hours and days (a sign of secondary bleeding), fever above 38.5 degrees, increasing redness with warmth or pus, shortness of breath, chest pain or a swollen, painful leg on one side (a sign of thrombosis or pulmonary embolism), sudden visual disturbance. Get in touch within days about any newly occurring weakness of facial expression and about any wound that opens.

Procedures in this region are often requested for a mixture of physical discomfort and aesthetic reasons. Good advice separates the two and clarifies whether a procedure is needed at all: the natural range in this area is very wide, and much of what is perceived as a deviation is normal.

A procedure changes the shape, not the sensation — and it may make sensation worse. Where discomfort during sport, when sitting or during sexual intercourse is the reason, that is an understandable ground. Where it is solely about an image created by comparison, a second conversation is worthwhile before operating.
Female intimate surgery
swelling, a feeling of pressure and pain for one to two weeks
bruising
temporarily altered sensation
restricted sitting and walking in the first few days
secondary bleeding or a collection of blood
infection or impaired wound healing in a region that is hard to keep dry
separation of the wound edges with delayed healing
permanently altered or reduced sensation
painful scars or scar tension, including during sexual intercourse
asymmetry or a result that does not match expectations
the need for a corrective procedure
general anaesthetic risks
Risks and limits of intimate surgery in women
Seek medical advice immediately in the event of: fever, increasing redness with warmth, pus, foul-smelling discharge, a wound that opens, pain that is getting worse, or persistent bleeding.

Procedures in this region are among the most delicate in this catalogue. Several of the procedures offered — in particular volume build-up with the patient's own fat, autologous blood treatments and shockwave therapy — are not supported by robust studies as to their effectiveness. At the same time the possible consequences of a complication are particularly far-reaching here. A urological assessment before each of these procedures is not a formality but a precondition.

For several procedures in this group no proof of effectiveness has been provided, and a lack of success is therefore a realistic outcome. A correction is considerably more difficult in this region than the first procedure. Obtain urological advice before deciding — including, and especially, from someone who does not offer the procedure.
Male intimate surgery
swelling, bruising and tenderness to pressure for one to three weeks
temporarily altered sensation
pain on erection during the healing phase
infection or impaired wound healing
secondary bleeding or a collection of blood
nodules, uneven distribution or hardened areas after fat transfer treatments
scarring with shortening or curvature
permanently altered or reduced sensation
erectile dysfunction
an unsatisfactory result requiring a corrective operation, which is more difficult than the first procedure
general anaesthetic risks
Risks and limits of intimate surgery in men
Seek medical help immediately in the event of: fever, increasing redness with warmth, pus, severe or increasing pain, problems passing water, persistent bleeding or a newly occurring hardened area.

Tightening procedures and liposuction on the body are the procedures with the highest risk of thrombosis in this catalogue — and it adds to the risk of a long flight home. That is why the clinic sets the date of the return flight, not your diary. Take that requirement seriously, even if you feel well.

Liposuction is not a means of losing weight and does not keep weight off. A tightening procedure removes skin, but it requires a stable weight and completed family planning, otherwise the result is largely gone after the next pregnancy or weight gain. Both procedures leave scars that remain.
Body
extensive bruising and swelling for weeks
numbness of the treated skin, frequently permanent below the navel after a tummy tuck
a feeling of tightness that forces a stooped posture for the first few days
long, permanent scars with tightening procedures
thrombosis and pulmonary embolism — the most serious risk with these procedures
a collection of fluid (seroma) that has to be drained several times; the most common complication after a tummy tuck
secondary bleeding or a collection of blood
impaired wound healing, particularly in the middle of the scar and particularly in smokers
dents, waves and contour irregularities after liposuction — the most common reason for corrective procedures
slack skin where too much volume has been removed
impaired blood supply to, or loss of, the newly positioned navel
fat embolism — rare, but serious
general anaesthetic risks
Risks and limits of body operations

Seek medical help immediately in the event of: shortness of breath, chest pain, a racing heart or a sudden cough (a sign of pulmonary embolism), a swollen, warm and painful leg on one side (a sign of thrombosis), fever above 38.5 degrees, rapidly increasing swelling, redness with warmth or pus, a wound that opens. These warning signs still apply weeks after the procedure and also at home in Switzerland — go to an emergency department with them, not to a scheduled appointment.
daten.risiken-gruppen.gruppen.zaehne/zah: The most important point in aesthetic dental treatment is rarely a medical risk but the irreversibility: the tooth substance that is removed does not come back, and a tooth that has been ground down needs a restoration permanently. The second point is aftercare: crowns, veneers and implants require lifelong monitoring — in Switzerland, with the corresponding cost.

An aesthetic restoration is no substitute for dental rehabilitation: caries, root inflammation and periodontitis belong treated beforehand, otherwise the work is done over the top of a problem. Ceramic is not a solution for ever — with crowns, veneers and implant crowns, reckon on a replacement after ten to fifteen years. And factor in the cost of the check-ups in Switzerland from the outset.
sensitivity to cold and heat for weeks
a feeling of pressure and irritation of the gums
swelling and bruising after surgical procedures
a period of getting used to the bite
death of the tooth nerve after grinding down, making root canal treatment necessary
receding gums with a visible crown margin
caries beneath the crown margin where the margin does not seal cleanly
chipping or fracture of the ceramic, particularly where teeth are ground at night
